intro: AI-safety practices written as asks a shareholder could make of a listed frontier lab (Anthropic; xAI through SpaceX) or of the companies that fund, host or supply labs. For each: who has committed to it, the rules that already require it, the nearest past proposals and their votes, the risk a company excludes it, and evidence that it is financially material. No shareholder proposal has yet asked a company for a frontier safety framework or dangerous-capability testing; the closest have asked for board oversight of AI.
about: Sources researched November 2026; vote shares are for ÷ (for + against) from each company's 8-K. Example wording is written by this site to adapt, not a recommendation, and nothing here says how anyone should vote.

asks.label: Publish and follow a frontier safety framework
asks.practice: Set out the capability thresholds at which risks become unacceptable, the safeguards each threshold triggers, and a commitment to pause development or deployment if the safeguards cannot be met.

committed.text: Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments (May 2024), signed by Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and xAI (Nvidia later): not to develop or deploy a model if its risks cannot be kept below the thresholds.
Published frameworks, indexed by METR: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI, Amazon, Microsoft and Nvidia. Oracle has none listed.

required_by.text: EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice, Safety and Security chapter (July 2025): a safety and security framework (Commitment 1).
California SB 53 (in force January 1, 2026): large frontier developers publish an annual framework.
New York RAISE Act (in force January 1, 2027): publish the framework, review it yearly, post material changes within 30 days; breaking it can be penalised.

asks.exclusion_risk: Low to moderate. Under the SEC's company-specific test for significance (Staff Legal Bulletin 14M, February 2025), catastrophic risk is plainly significant for a lab; the argument is weaker for a chip supplier. Since August 14, 2026 SEC staff no longer respond to exclusion requests, so a company decides and a proponent's remedy is a court.

materiality.text: Anthropic's prospectus says it has delayed, restricted or declined model releases under its safety policy, and lists this among risks to its competitive position.

asks.example: Shareholders request that the Board publish, and report annually on adherence to, a frontier AI safety framework specifying capability thresholds and required safeguards.
asks.precedents_note: None found in SEC full-text search of proxy statements and exempt solicitations, 2023 to November 2026.

asks.label: Test for dangerous capabilities before deployment, with outside testers
asks.practice: Before release, test models for chemical, biological, cyber and autonomy capabilities; publish results in system cards; and give independent and government evaluators access before release.

committed.text: Seoul commitments: internal and external red-teaming.

Anthropic gives pre-release access to the US government's AI evaluation body and the UK AI Security Institute (the prospectus's name for the US body differs from earlier usage; not confirmed which is current).
Alphabet's 2026 proxy statement names independent evaluators (Apollo Research, Vaultis, Dreadnode).

required_by.text: EU AI Act Article 55(1)(a): model evaluation including adversarial testing, for models with systemic risk (applicable from August 2, 2025).
EU Code of Practice Measure 3.5: independent external evaluators given free access.
California SB 53 and New York RAISE Act: transparency reports at deployment summarising risk assessments and the role of third-party evaluators.

asks.exclusion_risk: Low to moderate. A request for disclosure is judged by its underlying subject (Staff Legal Bulletin 14M); naming specific test protocols would raise the risk of exclusion as micromanagement.

materiality.text: Anthropic's prospectus reports 2026 incidents in which its models gained unauthorized access to systems during cyber evaluations, after which it suspended those evaluations.

asks.example: Shareholders request a report on pre-deployment dangerous-capability evaluations, including whether independent or government evaluators had pre-release access.
asks.precedents_note: None found in SEC full-text search of proxy statements and exempt solicitations, 2023 to November 2026.

asks.label: Independent assessment of compliance with the safety framework
asks.practice: Have a qualified outside party check whether the company actually follows its own safety framework, and publish a summary.

committed.text: Seoul commitments: explain how external actors are involved in assessing risk (no audit required).
Anthropic describes an external reviewer program and expects, with Accenture, to invest at least $1 billion each over five years in outside review capacity (terms not final).

required_by.text: EU Code of Practice Measure 8.1: external assurance where appropriate.
Not required by California SB 53, nor by New York's final RAISE Act text.

asks.exclusion_risk: Moderate. Requiring a named auditor or method could be called micromanagement; asking the board to commission an assessment and publish a summary is the safer framing.
asks.example: Shareholders request that the Board commission an independent assessment of compliance with the Company's frontier safety framework and publish a summary.
asks.precedents_note: None found in SEC full-text search of proxy statements and exempt solicitations, 2023 to November 2026.

asks.label: Secure model weights against theft
asks.practice: Protect unreleased model weights against outside attackers and insiders, under board oversight.

committed.text: Seoul commitments: cybersecurity and insider-threat safeguards for unreleased weights.

required_by.text: EU AI Act Article 55(1)(d): an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for models with systemic risk.
EU Code of Practice security measures, which cite RAND's work on securing model weights.
California SB 53: the framework must cover cybersecurity practices.

asks.exclusion_risk: Moderate to high. Cybersecurity detail is often argued to be ordinary business; frame the ask as board oversight and disclosure, not technical controls.

materiality.text: Anthropic's prospectus says it delayed a pre-training run by more than a month to strengthen protection against weight theft.
SpaceX's prospectus names model weights among intellectual property at risk from nation-state attackers.

asks.example: Shareholders request a report on Board oversight of measures to secure unreleased frontier model weights against theft.
asks.precedents_note: None found in SEC full-text search of proxy statements and exempt solicitations, 2023 to November 2026.

asks.label: Report serious AI incidents
asks.practice: Report serious AI incidents to regulators promptly, and publish summaries and the corrective action taken.

required_by.text: EU AI Act Article 55(1)(c): report serious incidents without undue delay.
EU Code of Practice Measure 9.3: deadlines of 2 to 15 days depending on the harm.
California SB 53: report to the state within 15 days, or 24 hours if there is imminent danger.
New York RAISE Act: within 72 hours.

asks.exclusion_risk: Low to moderate: reporting is now a legal duty, so a request to summarise it publicly is close to compliance disclosure.

materiality.text: Anthropic's prospectus cites the RAISE Act and SB 53 reporting duties as heightened compliance and liability exposure.
SpaceX's prospectus discloses investigations and lawsuits over xAI's Grok image generation.

asks.example: Shareholders request an annual report summarizing serious AI incidents reported to regulators and resulting corrective actions.
asks.precedents_note: None found in SEC full-text search of proxy statements and exempt solicitations, 2023 to November 2026.

asks.label: Protect employees who raise AI safety concerns
asks.practice: Let staff raise catastrophic-risk concerns with regulators without retaliation or gag clauses, through an anonymous channel.

committed.text: Not part of the Seoul commitments. Company policies were not reviewed (not confirmed).

required_by.text: California SB 53: anti-retaliation protection, notice to staff and an anonymous reporting channel.
EU Code of Practice Measure 8.3: no retaliation, and an annual notice to staff of the whistleblower policy.
Federal AI Whistleblower Protection Act (S.1792, introduced May 15, 2025): pending.

asks.exclusion_risk: Moderate. Workforce policy is classic ordinary business; a request to assess and disclose, rather than to adopt specific terms, is the safer framing.
asks.example: Shareholders request a report assessing whether Company policies allow employees to raise AI safety concerns with regulators without retaliation.
asks.precedents_note: None found in SEC full-text search of proxy statements and exempt solicitations, 2023 to November 2026.

asks.label: Board oversight of catastrophic AI risk
asks.practice: Give a named board committee responsibility for frontier and catastrophic AI risk, with directors who have relevant expertise.

committed.text: Anthropic has a board safety and risk committee of two independent directors overseeing the safety and security of its models, alongside its Long-Term Benefit Trust.

required_by.text: EU Code of Practice Measure 8.1: oversight by a committee of the board or an independent body.

precedents.text: Amazon 2024, Additional Board Committee to Oversee AI: 9.70% support.
Amazon 2025, Assessment of Board Structure for Oversight of AI: 10.27%.
Alphabet 2026, AI Board Oversight (update the Audit Committee charter): 3.74%.

asks.exclusion_risk: Low: proposals on board structure for AI oversight have reached the ballot at Amazon and Alphabet.

materiality.text: Amazon's 2024 opposition statement argued that none of its peers had a dedicated AI committee; Anthropic now has one.

asks.example: Shareholders request that the Board assign oversight of catastrophic frontier-AI risk to a committee and disclose its members' relevant expertise.

asks.label: Safety due diligence in investments, cloud and compute deals with labs
asks.practice: For hyperscalers and other investors in labs: report how the board weighs a lab's safety practices when investing in it or supplying it with large-scale compute.

committed.text: The October 2025 Microsoft and OpenAI agreement: any OpenAI declaration of AGI is to be verified by an independent expert panel; Microsoft holds about 27%.
Amazon's and Google's stakes in Anthropic are non-voting preferred stock; no public safety conditions found in those agreements (not confirmed).

required_by.text: No rule requires it. A November 2026 US export rule adds know-your-customer duties on remote access to advanced chips.

asks.exclusion_risk: Moderate to high. Contract terms are ordinary business and the micromanagement risk is real; ask for disclosure of board oversight, not specific contract terms.

materiality.text: Amazon's third-quarter 2026 report: upward adjustments to private investments of $62.9 billion in nine months, mainly its Anthropic preferred stock, plus a $5.0 billion further investment and a financing facility of up to $20 billion for Anthropic.

asks.example: Shareholders request a report on how the Board evaluates AI-safety practices of frontier labs in which the Company invests or to which it supplies large-scale compute.
asks.precedents_note: None found in SEC full-text search of proxy statements and exempt solicitations, 2023 to November 2026.

asks.label: Disclose spending on safety and alignment research
asks.practice: Disclose roughly what share of research compute and budget goes to safety and alignment.

committed.text: No lab publicly discloses a share. Anthropic says only that its compute goes to coding, agentic skills and safety research.

asks.exclusion_risk: Moderate to high. Allocating research spending is core ordinary business; asking for an approximate share to be disclosed, rather than a level of spending, is the safer framing.
asks.example: Shareholders request disclosure of the approximate share of AI research compute and budget devoted to safety and alignment research.
asks.precedents_note: None found in SEC full-text search of proxy statements and exempt solicitations, 2023 to November 2026.
